title: Making friends as you age
titleChinese: 随着年龄增长如何结交新朋友
paragraphs: At school you're surrounded by people your own age. Of course you spend a lot of time with them, and so some of the best friendships are forged at school. But later in life, it's easy to lose touch – you work full-time, maybe start a family, and your old friends might be scattered across the country or even the world. A 2016 study in Finland found that after the age of 25, the number of friends someone has falls very quickly, and this number continues to decrease throughout a person's life. So when you're in your mid-to-late 20s, how can you make new friends?

Radhika Sanghani, a BBC journalist, tasked herself with making new friends by saying 'yes' to any invitations that came her way. If a colleague asked her for lunch, she didn't shy away from it, and she soon made some of the closest friends she'd ever had. "We all message several times a week often leaving rambling voice notes; we host dinners at each other's houses; and we've all cried on each other at least once (the true mark of friendship)" she wrote in a 2018 article.

The website Talk Twenties recommends joining a local class or group, like taking up running or joining a choir. Having something in common gives you something to talk about with your new acquaintances, which will hopefully then translate into meaningful relationships. When you don't have mutual interests with someone, it can be difficult to get past the small talk stage, where conversation can quickly fizzle out, and a class can help avoid this.

Nowadays, there are also apps for meeting new people, like Bumble BFF or Meetup. Dr Robert Puff who writes for Psychology Today says solid friendships are essential for two main reasons. One is to help make life more enjoyable, and two is for support in difficult times – to make hardships more tolerable!
As we grow up, we can feel like we're not in control of what's happening around us, but we can control our social life, so enrich your life with fulfilling friendships.

vocabulary.entry: **forge** /fɔːdʒ/ v. 建立，形成（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The experience helped forge a strong bond between them.
vocabulary.translation: 这次经历帮助他们建立了牢固的联系。

vocabulary.entry: **lose touch** /ˌluːz ˈtʌtʃ/ phr. 失去联系（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: I lost touch with most of my school friends after university.
vocabulary.translation: 大学毕业后我和大多数校友失去了联系。

vocabulary.entry: **scattered** /ˈskætəd/ adj. 分散的，散布的
vocabulary.example: His family are scattered all over the world.
vocabulary.translation: 他的家人分散在世界各地。

vocabulary.entry: **task** /tɑːsk/ v. 交给……任务（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He tasked himself with finishing the report by Friday.
vocabulary.translation: 他给自己布置了在周五前完成报告的任务。

vocabulary.entry: **shy away from** /ˌʃaɪ əˈweɪ frəm/ phr. 回避，躲避（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: She never shies away from a challenge.
vocabulary.translation: 她从不回避挑战。

vocabulary.entry: **rambling** /ˈræmblɪŋ/ adj. 冗长而杂乱的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He sent me a rambling email that went on for pages.
vocabulary.translation: 他给我发了一封冗长杂乱的电子邮件，洋洋洒洒好几页。

vocabulary.entry: **voice note** /ˈvɔɪs nəʊt/ n. 语音留言（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: She left me a voice note instead of texting.
vocabulary.translation: 她给我留了一条语音留言而不是发短信。

vocabulary.entry: **acquaintance** /əˈkweɪntəns/ n. 熟人，相识的人（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He has many acquaintances but few close friends.
vocabulary.translation: 他认识很多人，但亲密朋友很少。

vocabulary.entry: **translate into** /trænsˈleɪt ɪntə/ phr. 转化为，导致（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Hard work doesn't always translate into success.
vocabulary.translation: 努力工作并不总是转化为成功。

vocabulary.entry: **mutual** /ˈmjuːtʃuəl/ adj. 共同的，相互的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: They discovered a mutual interest in music.
vocabulary.translation: 他们发现彼此对音乐有共同的兴趣。

vocabulary.entry: **small talk** /ˈsmɔːl tɔːk/ n. 闲聊，寒暄（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: We made small talk about the weather while waiting for the meeting to start.
vocabulary.translation: 我们一边等待会议开始，一边闲聊天气。

vocabulary.entry: **fizzle out** /ˌfɪzl ˈaʊt/ phr. v. 无疾而终，虎头蛇尾（口语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The party fizzled out after midnight.
vocabulary.translation: 派对在午夜后渐渐冷清下来。

vocabulary.entry: **solid** /ˈsɒlɪd/ adj. 牢固的，可靠的
vocabulary.example: They have a solid marriage.
vocabulary.translation: 他们的婚姻很牢固。

vocabulary.entry: **essential** /ɪˈsenʃl/ adj. 必不可少的，本质的
vocabulary.example: A good diet is essential for everyone.
vocabulary.translation: 良好的饮食对每个人都至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: **enjoyable** /ɪnˈdʒɔɪəbl/ adj. 令人愉快的，有乐趣的
vocabulary.example: We had a very enjoyable evening.
vocabulary.translation: 我们度过了一个非常愉快的夜晚。

vocabulary.entry: **hardship** /ˈhɑːdʃɪp/ n. 艰难，困苦（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The refugees have endured great hardship.
vocabulary.translation: 难民们承受了巨大的苦难。

vocabulary.entry: **tolerable** /ˈtɒlərəbl/ adj. 可忍受的，可容忍的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The pain was just tolerable.
vocabulary.translation: 疼痛尚可忍受。

vocabulary.entry: **enrich** /ɪnˈrɪtʃ/ v. 丰富，充实（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Reading enriches the mind.
vocabulary.translation: 阅读充实心灵。

vocabulary.entry: **fulfilling** /fʊlˈfɪlɪŋ/ adj. 令人满意的，有成就感的
vocabulary.example: She finds her work very fulfilling.
vocabulary.translation: 她觉得自己的工作很有成就感。

vocabulary.entry: **colleague** /ˈkɒliːɡ/ n. 同事
vocabulary.example: I discussed the problem with my colleagues.
vocabulary.translation: 我和同事们讨论了这个问题。

vocabulary.entry: **choir** /ˈkwaɪə(r)/ n. 合唱团，唱诗班
vocabulary.example: She sings in the school choir.
vocabulary.translation: 她在学校合唱团唱歌。

vocabulary.entry: **decrease** /dɪˈkriːs/ v. 减少，下降
vocabulary.example: The number of students has decreased this year.
vocabulary.translation: 今年学生人数减少了。

vocabulary.entry: **mid-to-late 20s** /ˌmɪd tə ˌleɪt ˈtwentiz/ phr. 二十多岁中后期（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: People in their mid-to-late 20s often face career decisions.
vocabulary.translation: 二十多岁中后期的人常常面临职业决策。

vocabulary.entry: **surrounded** /səˈraʊndɪd/ adj. 被……环绕的
vocabulary.example: She likes to be surrounded by friends and family.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢被朋友和家人环绕。

vocabulary.entry: **invitation** /ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃn/ n. 邀请
vocabulary.example: She received an invitation to the wedding.
vocabulary.translation: 她收到了婚礼邀请。

sentences.english: At school you're surrounded by people your own age.
sentences.chinese: 在学校，你身边都是同龄人。

sentences.english: A 2016 study in Finland found that after the age of 25, the number of friends someone has falls very quickly, and this number continues to decrease throughout a person's life.

sentences.english: So when you're in your mid-to-late 20s, how can you make new friends?
sentences.chinese: 那么，当你处于二十多岁中后期时，如何才能结交新朋友呢？

sentences.english: Radhika Sanghani, a BBC journalist, tasked herself with making new friends by saying 'yes' to any invitations that came her way.
sentences.chinese: BBC记者拉迪卡·桑哈尼给自己定下任务，对任何找上门的邀请都说"好"，以此结交新朋友。

sentences.english: If a colleague asked her for lunch, she didn't shy away from it, and she soon made some of the closest friends she'd ever had.
sentences.chinese: 如果有同事约她吃午饭，她不会回避，很快她就交到了一些她有史以来最亲密的朋友。"

sentences.chinese: 我们每周都会发几次消息，经常留下冗长的语音留言；我们在彼此家里举办晚餐聚会；而且我们至少都在对方面前哭过一次（友谊的真正标志），"她在2018年的一篇文章中写道。

sentences.chinese: 网站"二十多岁交谈"建议加入当地的课程或团体，比如开始跑步或加入合唱团。

sentences.chinese: 如今，也有用于结识新朋友的应用程序，比如Bumble BFF或Meetup。

sentences.english: Dr Robert Puff who writes for Psychology Today says solid friendships are essential for two main reasons.
sentences.chinese: 为《今日心理学》撰稿的罗伯特·帕夫博士说，牢固的友谊至关重要，主要有两个原因。

sentences.english: One is to help make life more enjoyable, and two is for support in difficult times – to make hardships more tolerable!
sentences.chinese: 一是帮助让生活更愉快，二是在困难时期提供支持——让艰难时刻更易于忍受！

sentences.chinese: 随着我们长大，我们可能会觉得自己无法控制周围发生的事情，但我们可以控制自己的社交生活，所以要用令人满意的友谊来丰富你的生活。
